Expiry Policy

1. What is an Expiry Policy?
  • An expiry policy defines how long data entries live in the cache before they are automatically removed;
  • It follows the JCache (JSR 107) ExpiryPolicy interface;
  • Entries are removed after the expiry duration, freeing up memory;
2. Expiry Triggers
  • Created — TTL starts when the entry is first added to the cache;
  • Accessed — TTL resets every time the entry is read;
  • Updated — TTL resets every time the entry is modified;
3. Built-in Expiry Policies
PolicyExpires After
CreatedExpiryPolicyA fixed duration after creation
AccessedExpiryPolicyA fixed duration after last access
ModifiedExpiryPolicyA fixed duration after last modification
TouchedExpiryPolicyA fixed duration after last access or modification
EternalExpiryPolicyNever (default)
4. Configuring Expiry Policy
  • At cache level: 
    CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("sessionCache");
cfg.setExpiryPolicyFactory(
    CreatedExpiryPolicy.factoryOf(new Duration(TimeUnit.MINUTES, 30))
);
  • Per operation (using withExpiryPolicy): 
    ExpiryPolicy policy = new CreatedExpiryPolicy(new Duration(TimeUnit.HOURS, 1));

cache.withExpiryPolicy(policy).put(key, value);
5. Eager TTL
  • By default, eagerTtl is true — Ignite actively scans for and removes expired entries;
  • If set to false, expired entries are only removed when accessed (lazy expiration);
  • Eager TTL uses a background thread; disable it if you have very many caches and expiry is not critical;
